title: Premier League 2026-27 preview No 13: Leeds | Premier League previews 2026-27 | The Guardian
description: After keeping Leeds up last season and reaching an FA Cup semi-final, Daniel Farke has good reason to expect further improvement at Elland Road
Author: Louise Taylor
Headline: After keeping Leeds up last season and reaching an FA Cup semi-final, Daniel Farke has good reason to expect further improvement at Elland Road
Content: Lukas Nmecha celebrates after his goal during the pre-season friendly match between Sunderland AFC and Leeds United  Photograph: Rebekah Wynkoop/SPP/ShutterstockAfter keeping Leeds up last season and reaching an FA Cup semi-final, Daniel Farke has good reason to expect further improvement at Elland RoadByLouise TaylorMon 17 Aug 2026 19.01 EDTLast modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 19.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGuardian writers’ predicted position:12th (NB: this is not necessarily Louise Taylor’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)Last season’s position:14thProspectsPretty bright. A team’s second season in thePremier Leaguefollowing promotion is traditionally regarded as hazardous but all the indications are that Daniel Farke’s side will not merely harbour a high degree of immunity to this syndrome but could debunk it as a lazy cliche. The spine of the side looks extremely robust and has been reinforced by the club record £40m signing of James Trafford from Manchester City and the £34m acquisition of the Bosnia and Herzegovina centre-half Tarik Muharemovic from Sassuolo.Much hinges on Dominic Calvert-Lewin remaining fit. At times last season, Farke’s centre-forward proved unplayable as Leeds finished a respectable 14th. This time round Calvert-Lewin and his fellow forwards should benefit from assists provided by the talented Harry Wilson, a free transfer recruit from Fulham.Significantly, survival was achieved last spring after an unconvincing start to the campaign that, by November, had placed Farke’s job in jeopardy. After a switch to a, broadly, 3-5-2 formation the team improved, radically. Indeed, were there a separate Premier League table for the second half of the season, Leeds’ form from the start of December would have left them seventh. Pre-season results can be notoriously misleading but it is worth noting that Leeds have impressed against some strong opposition. “Pre-season has given us confidence,” said Farke.While the manager aims to take Leeds to “a new level” such ambition is tempered by sensible caution. “Everyone is talking of Europe and trophies but it’s important we stay humble and grounded,” he said. “In the last 25 years our highest Premier League finish has been ninth so we need to go step by step. The second year after promotion can be difficult and dangerous but we are hopeful we can have a good season.”Past fiveOff-field pictureThe dated, if hugely atmospheric, Elland Road is undergoing a wholesale redevelopment in a project instigated by the club’s owners, 49ers Enterprises, the investment arm of the NFL’s San Francisco 49ers. One of the ideas behind this much-needed stadium modernisation – involving an increase in capacity from 37,792 to 53,000 – is to help increase commercial revenue streams and, in turn, be less restricted by football’s spending rules. Another priority is reducing the lengthy season ticket waiting list. Elland Road should remain fully operational on match days as work progresses on a design intended to be the centrepiece of a wider local regeneration. The only frustration is that city council plans for a new tram network have once again been heavily delayed. With public transport infrastructure poor in a part of Leeds notorious for serious traffic congestion that could prove a big problem on match days at an expanded arena.Owner-fan relationshipDecent. Leeds have had some unpredictable owners in recent years so the sense of stability, professionalism and vision introduced by the California-based 49ers Enterprises has been welcome. With Elland Road now in the process of being redeveloped, Trafford recently becoming the club’s record signing and commercial income being boosted appreciably, few doubt the ownership’s ambition. A senior executive team comprising chair, Paraag Marathe, managing director, Robbie Evans, and sporting director, Adam Underwood, is generally regarded as efficient, sensible and sufficiently realistic to remain on the right side of football’s spending rules.The managerFarke says his personality is “95% coffee and cake on the sofa and 5% fire beast”. An economics graduate who originally intended to become a sporting director, the 49-year-old one time lower division German striker and, later, Norwich manager is an interesting, multi-dimensional character with an engaging sense of humour and a love of literary fiction. In steering then newly promoted Leeds to the safety of 14thposition last season while also reaching an FA Cup semi-final, Farke lost the “trampoline man” tag that, rather unfairly, had suggested his career largely involved either winning promotion or facing relegation. A coach close to Pep Guardiola, Jürgen Klopp and Thomas Tuchel has described himself as “a football romantic who has learned that romanticism shouldn’t blind you to reality”. As he explains: “My brand of football normally suits teams who dominate possession but I’m always switched on to what is necessary.”Star signingView image in fullscreenTarik Muharemovic comes in from Serie A to bolster the Leeds defence.Photograph: Richard Bierton/Every Second Media/ShutterstockThe 23-year-old left-sided central defender Muharemovic has looked outstanding in pre-season. The £34m signing from Serie A has imbued Farke’s defence with not merely robust physicality and controlled aggression but assurance on the ball and a refined passing range. The manner in which he bundled Sunderland’s formidable Netherlands centre-forward Brian Brobbey over in pre-season delighted Leeds fans who have already labelled him the Bosnian King. After helping Sassuolo win promotion from Serie B, Muharemovic played a big part in securing a mid-table Serie A finish last season. Comfortable in a back three or a back four, he appears an inspired reinforcement for a team that, further forward, also seem likely to benefit from Wilson’s arrival.Set for a breakthroughIn recruiting Trafford, Leeds pulled off quite a coup. The 23-year-old England goalkeeper, currently understudy to Jordan Pickford in Tuchel’s squad, shone at Burnley in the Championship and arguably deserved more than to be No 2 at City last term. Trafford’s excellence with his feet can only enhance Farke’s team and his all-round talent and impressive poise under pressure should guarantee Leeds some invaluable extra points. All the indications are that the son of a Cumbrian farmer who still tries to lend a hand at lambing time is about to show the world how good he really is.World Cup impactAlthough the versatile forward ended last season in fine form for Leeds, Noah Okafor played just 25 minutes as a substitute – against Algeria – as Switzerland reached the quarter-finals, eventually bowing out to Argentina. Given Okafor’s previous rift with Murat Yakin, Switzerland’s head coach, there was a degree of surprise when he was included in his World Cup squad and it appears he had not done quite enough to earn Yakin’s full trust. Despite making one appearance for the United States as they reached the last 16 it was still a good summer for Brenden Aaronson. Farke’s trusted attacking midfielder briefly left the US pre-tournament training camp in late May and returned a married man after his long-planned wedding to Milana D’Ambra.Explore more on these topicsPremier League previews 2026-27Leeds UnitedPremier LeaguefeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Rubin Colwill’s last-gasp free-kick earns Cardiff dramatic point against Wrexham | Championship | The Guardian
description: Rubin Colwill’s stoppage-time equaliser earned Cardiff a 1-1 draw with Welsh rivals Wrexham after Kieffer Moore had given the visitors a third-minute lead
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Rubin Colwill’s stoppage-time equaliser earned Cardiff a 1-1 draw with Welsh rivals Wrexham after Kieffer Moore had given the visitors a third-minute lead
Content: Rubin Colwill’s free-kick heads for the back of the net as Cardiff snatch a point deep into added time.Photograph: Kieran McManus/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenRubin Colwill’s free-kick heads for the back of the net as Cardiff snatch a point deep into added time.Photograph: Kieran McManus/ShutterstockChampionshipRubin Colwill’s last-gasp free-kick earns Cardiff dramatic point against WrexhamPA MediaMon 17 Aug 2026 17.32 EDTLast modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 18.51 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRubin Colwill scored a ferocious equaliser with almost the final kick of the match to earn Cardiff a 1-1Championshipdraw with Wrexham.Wrexham appeared to have the Welsh derby bragging rights sewn up as the contest ticked into the eighth minute of added time atCardiff CityStadium.Flemming’s dramatic Burnley double pegs back West Ham on Championship returnRead moreBut George Dobson brought down Joel Colwill on the edge of the box, and his brother Rubin stepped up to lash a brilliant free-kick over the wall and past Anthony Patterson in theWrexhamgoal.Colwill’s strike cancelled out Kieffer Moore’s third-minute effort, the former Cardiff forward continuing his habit of scoring against his former employers – his seventh goal against the Bluebirds.Wrexham had 18 goal attempts to 11 and, in truth, should have prevented any late anxiety by putting the game beyond the hosts back at this level after a season in League One.Cardiff’s defensive resources had been stretched by injuries to Calum Chambers, Dylan Lawlor and Will Fish, so much so that the usual left-back Joel Bagan was switched inside to partner Gabriel Osho in the heart of defence.The new-look partnership was exposed immediately after Cardiff only managed to clear a Lewis O’Brien free-kick as far as Danny Imray, and his ball forward caught the hosts napping.Osho played Moore onside and the striker broke beyond Bagan to rifle the ball above Nathan Trott’s head for his first goal since February, ending his run of 11 Wrexham games without scoring.Trott tipped over Callum Doyle’s header as Cardiff appeared to struggle to get to grips with the pace of Championship football. But the Bluebirds slowly improved and had a good spell midway through the first half after Zak Vyner left a back pass short and Patterson reacted smartly to beat Yousef Salech to the loose ball.View image in fullscreenWrexham’s Kieffer Moore roars in delight after giving his side an early lead at Cardiff.Photograph: Nick Potts/PAJack Moylan then scooped over and Patterson made a comfortable save from Cian Ashford after some slick Cardiff passing.Wrexham went close to a second when Moore rose well from an O’Brien cross and skimmed the crossbar with a header. Imray’s scuffed shot then forced a save from Trott, although the ball appeared to be heading wide anyway.Just as they had at the start of the game, Cardiff switched off after the restart. Ollie Rathbone’s ball inside found Doyle, but Trott was alive at the near post to save with his foot. Trott made a more comfortable stop from Nathan Broadhead before Doyle lashed a rasping drive past him and on to a post.Cardiff sent on the Colwill brothers just after the hour mark to try to shift momentum in their favour, and Moylan saw his deflected effort drift just wide.Dominic Hyam headed against his own crossbar, but Cardiff kept pushing and ultimately denied Wrexham their first win in the Welsh capital since 1992.Explore more on these topicsChampionshipCardiff CityWrexhammatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Rodri calls it ‘a dream to play for Barcelona’ as he flies in for medical | Transfer window | The Guardian
description: Rodri said it is ‘a dream’ to play for Barcelona after landing in Catalonia on Monday to complete his move from Manchester City
Author: Mark Dobson
Headline: Rodri said it is ‘a dream’ to play for Barcelona after landing in Catalonia on Monday to complete his move from Manchester City
Content: Rodri waves to fans as he lands in Barcelona to complete his move from Manchester City.Photograph: Alejandro García/EPAView image in fullscreenRodri waves to fans as he lands in Barcelona to complete his move from Manchester City.Photograph: Alejandro García/EPATransfer windowRodri calls it ‘a dream to play for Barcelona’ as he flies in for medicalSpain midfielder in £65.4m move from Manchester City‘I’m happy that everything has been resolved’Mark DobsonMon 17 Aug 2026 15.39 EDTFirst published on Sun 16 Aug 2026 16.46 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleRodri has said it is “a dream” to play for Barcelona after landing in Catalonia on Monday to complete his move fromManchester City. Spain’s World Cup-winning captain will have a medical on Tuesday after City accepted Barcelona’s third bid of £65.4m.“Very happy to arrive,” Rodri said at Barcelona’s El Prat airport. “There have been some very intense days, but I’m happy that everything has been resolved. For me it’s a dream to play forBarcelona. I’m excited about being with my teammates, many of them I already know. Now it’s time to get to work and give my best.”Sergio’s stunner lights up El Sardinero on Racing Santander’s emotional La Liga return | Sid LoweRead moreThe 30-year-old had entered the final year of his contract at the Etihad Stadium and made it clear he would like the opportunity to move to Barcelona. City, who are now closing in on a deal to sign Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, were reluctant sellers but had little choice with Rodri out of contract next summer.City had already rejected Barcelona’s bid of around €60m (£51m) for Rodri last week after an initial offer of €45m (£38.5m) but have now accepted the latest bid.Speaking after City’s 3-0 Community Shielddefeat by Arsenalon Sunday, Enzo Maresca called Rodri a “top player” and said “all the teams need Rodri”, but City have been unable to persuade their linchpin to stay and sign a new contract. Rodri had only returned to the club on Friday, having undergone back surgery after the World Cup, with Maresca saying he had given him a “big hug” when he first met up with him.Rodri has spent seven seasons with City, winning the Premier League four times and scoring the only goal when they beat Inter in the2023 Champions League final. The following year he won the Ballon d’Or but, by the time he was presented with the trophy, he was sidelined with an anterior cruciate ligament which ruled him out of most of the 2024-25 campaign, while hamstring and groin problems limited him to 33 appearances in Pep Guardiola’s final campaign in charge.City have already undergone major changes in midfield this summer, spending £116m on Elliot Anderson, while agreeing a deal to sell Tijjani Reijnders to Al Qadsiah. They are now ready to seal a move for the Morocco star Bouaddi.The teenager impressed at the World Cup and Lille had initially wanted any potential move to include a 12-month loan deal back to the French side. However, with City losing Bernardo Silva and now Rodri, Maresca is keen to bulk up his midfield options for the new campaign and want Bouaddi available for this season. City have also been linked with Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández and retain an interest.Explore more on these topicsTransfer windowBarcelonaManchester CitynewsShareReuse this content

title: Sergio’s stunner lights up El Sardinero on Racing Santander’s emotional La Liga return | La Liga | The Guardian
description: Teenager’s glorious strike made it 2-0 against Villarreal – but though they were pegged back to a draw the match sealed a feelgood return from the abyss
Author: Sid Lowe
Headline: Teenager’s glorious strike made it 2-0 against Villarreal – but though they were pegged back to a draw the match sealed a feelgood return from the abyss
Content: Sergio Martínez wheels away after his 34th-minute goal – on arrival at the corner flag the gravity of his achievement suddenly struck him.Photograph: Europa Press Sports/Europa Press/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenSergio Martínez wheels away after his 34th-minute goal – on arrival at the corner flag the gravity of his achievement suddenly struck him.Photograph: Europa Press Sports/Europa Press/Getty ImagesLa LigaSergio’s stunner lights up El Sardinero on Racing Santander’s emotional La Liga returnTeenager’s glorious strike made it 2-0 against Villarreal – but though they were pegged back to a draw the match sealed a feelgood return from the abyssSid LoweMon 17 Aug 2026 13.15 EDTLast modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 15.36 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google“The poor kid couldn’t believe what had happened; none of us could have if we’d just done what he had just done,” said Álvaro Mantilla, Racing Santander’s captain in the match they had longed for more than anything in the world. Which was why the kid – a 19-year-old from just along the coast who had been at the club half his life – wasn’t the only one crying. The day Sergio Martínez played his first game for Racing, he had climbed into the stand to hug his grandad; the day he played his first inprimera, on Sunday afternoon at the Sardinero, he just about managed to stand before it, legs giving way a little and tears coming to his eyes. All around him they felt it too, 22,413 people absolutely losing it.What he had just done was, well, everything. At least that’s how it felt right then. “Euphoria”, his captain called it. In his first game in the first division, his third start ever, Sergio hadn’t just scored; he had scored the kind of goal you get in a comic, all explosions and exclamation marks. The ball sat up like an invitation andKapow!– Sergio smashed it on the bounce, a cartoon arrow drawn to the top corner. It tore through the air and through time, flashing past at 126km an hour and 14 years a second, so Sergio ran to the corner, holding the badge he has worn since he was 10. There, there was a wobble as it came to him just what he had done. Bloody hell, this was actually happening.La Liga 2026-27 preview: Madrid look to Mourinho in bid to dethrone BarcelonaRead moreThe teenager won’t even remember the last time Racing were in the first division: he was five. This was not just Sergio’s first top-flight game, it was Mantilla’s too – he was born and raised 5km away. And it was Jorge Salinas’ first as well, another 19-year-old from Santander. Sergio Canales, an academy kid from Santander like them, had played there and with Racing but that was 16 years ago, when he was a teenager too,the most eligible in Spain. Thirty-five now, he had at last come home. In almost the entire time he had been away, so had his club. Sunday afternoon was the first time that Racing, founder members of the first division, had played a top-flight game since 2012. And here they were 2-0 up against Villarreal, the redemption real.It didn’t last long but it will last for a very, very long time. Leading 1-0 through a penalty from Andrés Martín, Sergio made it 2-0 in the 34th minute. They had deserved it too: “The energy was unstoppable,” Villarreal coach Iñigo Pérez admitted. For 44 minutes, Racing were something like perfection. And then in 67 seconds, two flashes from Pape Gueye and Nicholas Pépé had taken it away again – a reminder, Racing’s coach José Alberto López said, of what the first division is, how unforgiving it can be. Except this wasn’t going to be taken away: not the point, a 2-2 draw against the team that finished third last season which could be decisive in what will surely still be a fight for survival, and not the moment, their day.View image in fullscreenTeenager Sergio Martínez extended Racing Santander’s lead before being pegged back by Villarreal.Photograph: Cesar Ortiz Gonzalez/NurPhoto/ShutterstockEl Sardinero, more ground than stadium, built in the late 1980s and with something about it that’s happily still there with corner floodlights touching the sky, was packed again. Along the waterfront they had come, the only people not in white Racing shirts those in green ones: a city, a community built, heading back to where they belong. If they were home, so was the first division: this was one of those days that everyone else could celebrate too. “I loved it,” said Pérez, and he coaches their opponents. “I’m so happy to come here and see all the emotion and the excitement. This is a joy for anyone who comes.” But more than a historic club being in the first division for the first time since 2012, this was aboutbeing, full stop.Relegated in 2012 after a decade in the top flight, having played in Europejust three and a half years earlierandbeaten Manchester City along the way, Racing fell a long way, and might never have got up again.At all.They were relegated again immediately and spent seven of the next 10 years in Segunda B, Spain’s theoretically amateur third-to-seventh-tier with its 80 teams and four groups. Worse, their fight for survival was not just about sport. By then, the financial and institutional crisis was out of control. The debt had reached over €40m. €14m was owed to the state and players and staff went unpaid. In July 2011 they filed for bankruptcy,opening up an administration process. In an era when the club’s shirt sponsor was for a brand of chorizo, slang for thief, two presidents would eventually get jail sentences for embezzlement of club funds – and thatdoesn’tinclude Ahsan Ali Syed.Francisco Pernía and Ángel Lavín were the men charged. Between them came “Mr Ali”, welcomed as a saviour in the winter of 2011, championed by Pernía and the leader of the Cantabrian government, Miguel Ángel Revilla, who declared: “The Hindu has his pockets full of cash.” Ali spent €3.5m on the buyout and said there was space alongside Real Madrid and Barcelona for Racing. Instead they ended up in a league with Langreo, Durango and Calahorra. He, meanwhile,had disappeared entirely, wanted by Interpol and finally arrested almost a decade later for fraud.View image in fullscreenJorge Salinas, 19, was another young Racing Santander making his La Liga debut.Photograph: Cesar Ortiz Gonzalez/NurPhoto/ShutterstockWith Lavín taking over, Racing’s crisis deepened, the sense that the end was coming. In January 2014, fans stormed the directors’ box and tried to force Lavín out. Then, a fortnight later, their players walked on to the pitch for the quarter-finals of the Copa del Rey against Real Sociedad. Still in Segunda B, they had beaten two first division sides but instead of playing they just stood there with their arms around each other’s shoulders. There was a dignity in their defiance, a solidarity.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWith Lavín at last forced out, former player Manolo Higuera stepping in in 2015, there was the start of a revival: a decency, an honesty, a seriousness about confronting their reality. Something was forged by being on the edge too, but they hadn’t stepped back from it entirely. When club legend Pedro Munitis became coach in 2015, it wasn’t just that he wasn’t paid, it was that he, like others at the club, waspaying: players’ wages, and even travel costs were coming out of his pocket. More than 50 legal cases still hung over them. The club was “dead and buried”, Higuera admits, little they could do; that they came through it was “a miracle”. They only played one of the next three seasons in the second division and although they went up in 2022, when José Alberto López took over as coach that December, there was a risk that they would slip back down again. Instead, he secured survival. Then seventh, then a playoff place, and then the title.José Alberto said that to begin with Racing were still closer to being an amateur side, “more neighbourhood team than professional club”. He admitted that he wondered what he had got himself into, but he helped them get out of it. Having been forced to give up playing at 20 because of rheumatism, José Alberto had begun at the bottom, working at Ikea while he coached in Asturias; now his approach carried Racing. Brave and attacking, his team would go for opponents; this was going to be fun too, that was non-negotiable. Even last year when they won the second division, they conceded 61 goals. A momentum built that would eventually bring them up. Optimism was back at last, on and off the pitch.Quick GuideLa Liga results and fixturesShowAlavés 3-0 Getafe, Espanyol 3-0 Levante, Racing Santander 2-2 Villarreal, Sevilla 2-1 Rayo VallecanoMondayDeportivo La Coruña v Elche (8pm BST)WednesdayAtlético Madrid v Malaga (8pm BST)Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.That summer Higuera convinced Sebastián Ceria to get involved. The time was right: Ceria, a social democrat Argentinian philanthropist with a PhD in mathematics from Carnegie and a professor at Columbia, had just sold his company for $850m. His wife, Alicia Zorrilla, is from Cantabria and friends with Higuera’s wife. Ceria bought a controlling stake for €30m, bringing a new mentality built around the people – and above all stability. In December 2024, the final administration payments were met, their debts paid off 13 years on. Assets that had been stripped have been recovered, so too has the pride, a sense of belonging. With Ceria describing football as “democratising”, the shift is visible in the shirts all across the city.It had started with a lunch in London. This Sunday Higuera and Ceria sat in the stand at the Sardinero together and watched Racing Santander play in the first division once again. And they watched the side play the way the coach that transformed them always said they would: no backing down, no doubt thatprimerais their place too. They saw the flags along the roof – every first division team there, them too – and heard the fans belt outLa Fuente de Cachoat the start of the day they had waited a lifetime for. They saw fans lead the way alongside the Cantabrian sea and Mantilla lead the way out of the tunnel, armband on. They saw Sergio announce his arrival and all of theirs, not alone in feeling the tears. And Canales, who had announced his departure at the same age, standing before supporters singing songs of redemption and return. “It was … strange,” Canales said, somehow speaking for all of them too. “I can’t quite assimilate this still. I could feel the hairs standing on end. Above all, what I feel is gratitude.”PosTeamPGDPts1Alaves1332Espanyol1333Sevilla1134Racing Santander1015Villarreal1016Athletic Bilbao0007Atletico Madrid0008Barcelona0009Celta Vigo00010Deportivo La Coruna00011Elche00012Malaga00013Osasuna00014Real Betis00015Real Madrid00016Real Sociedad00017Valencia00018Rayo Vallecano1-1019Getafe1-3020Levante1-30Explore more on these topicsLa LigaRacing SantanderEuropean club footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Pocognoli looks the part as Scotland’s new boss but a question remains: can he boogie?  | Soccer | The Guardian
description: In today’s Football Daily: Fitba, scooters on the pitch, and more
Author: Rob Smyth
Headline: In today’s Football Daily: Fitba, scooters on the pitch, and more
Content: Sébastien Pocognoli at his Scotland unveiling at Hampden, complete with vintage foot-on-the-ball pose.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PAView image in fullscreenSébastien Pocognoli at his Scotland unveiling at Hampden, complete with vintage foot-on-the-ball pose.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PAFootball Daily newsletterSoccerPocognoli looks the part as Scotland’s new boss but a question remains: can he boogie?Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!Rob SmythMon 17 Aug 2026 10.33 EDTLast modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 11.09 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFICKLE FITBAWhen Berti Vogts was unveiled as Scotland’s first foreign manager, back in 2002,he had a simple instruction. “When we are playing,” he said, “you can call me Berti McVogts!” Scotland fans preferred a slightly courser sobriquet when, six months later, Scotland went 2-0 down to the Faroe Islands beforescrambling a 2-2 draw. Vogts left after two-and-a-half ultimately unsuccessful years, and since then Scotland have preferred homegrown managers. But it’s good to try everything twice, except maybeGigli, and the Scottish FA has appointed one of European football’s most interesting young managers: Sébastien Pocognoli, who wasunveiled at a press conferenceon Monday.It’s 2026, not 2002, and the way to win people over is with a PowerPoint presentation rather than a cheesy pun. So even though Pocognoli’s middle name, Jean, gave him a bit of a portmanteau open goal, he didn’t ask to be called Jockognoli. Pocognoli, 39, is a former Belgium international who played for West Brom and Brighton. He had a glorious start to his senior coaching career in 2024-25 when he led Union Saint-Gilloise to their first Belgian title since 1935. His head was soon hunted by Monaco, who dispensed it in the summer after a disappointing season. Although Monaco finished seventh, their lowest position since 2019-20, Pocognoli’s win percentage of 42 wasn’t a complete affront to the memory of Tim Sherwood.“I’m very proud to be here,” roared Pocognoli. “Scotland is a passionate country and I think also, regarding the strong foundation that Steve Clarke and his staff did, that I can use this heritage to put the next accent in the style of play while also developing players for the future.” Pocognoli looked the part: sharp suit, art-dealer haircut, beard that has been through at least three focus groups to find the optimum length. He looked a bit like a cross between Diego Simeone and Gerard Piqué, which would be a helluva style of play to master.“Since negotiations began, I have been doing a lot of research, asking a lot of questions and looking at areas that we can build on,” continued Pocognoli, who confirmed that Barry Can’t Swim and Limmy would be joining his coaching staff. Craig Mulholland, the SFA’s chief football suit, said Pocognoli “will bring an aggressive, front-foot style of play that will excite supporters”. For all the Scotland fans who wanted to feel their pulse while watching Clarke’s side, the next few years will provide either told-you-so validation or football’s latest reminder that you should be careful what you wish for.QUOTE OF THE DAY“FIRST TIME EVER. Game delayed due to a child who’s scootered their way on to the pitch. Fair play to the Rangers manager for stopping the game and Charlie Elliott taking her back to her parent” –Montrose FC’s liveupdates on their SPWPL opener against Rangers – a 4-1 win for the Glaswegians – were briefly interrupted by news of a rogue fan with absolutely zero respect for the rules.View image in fullscreenRangers manager Leanne Crichton (centre) was on hand to help a young fan (scooter and child presumably just out of shot).Photograph: Luke Nickerson/Rangers FC/ShutterstockFOOTBALL DAILY LETTERSdouble quotation markWatching Manchester City under new management for the first time, it’s kind of spooky how much Enzo Maresca channels the ghost of Pep Guardiola on the touchline. Except they are losing” – Chris Jersan.double quotation markDave Hill’s letter [Friday’s Football Daily] made me feel old. My immediate reaction was: ‘Too much money sloshing around at the top; there should be a salary cap.’ Then I realised that I could just about remember the campaign for aminimumwage for footballers. All in the span of one lifetime” – Trevor Townson.double quotation markRe: your mention in Friday’s Football Daily of Graeme Souness being sent off in the first half of his first game as Rangers player-manager v Hibs. This event led to pubs popular with Celtic fans in the east end of Glasgow being inundated with requests for a new drink: ‘I’ll have a Souness please … mine’s a half and then I’m off’” – Danny Sullivan.If you have any, please send letters tothe.boss@theguardian.com.Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day winner is … Danny Sullivan. title: Sydney Swans coach ‘extremely disappointed’ as club faces call on standing down players linked to alleged sexual assault | AFL | The Guardian
description: Victoria police investigating allegation of sexual assault in the early hours of Monday morning at a Melbourne hotel
Author: Jack Snape
Headline: Victoria police investigating allegation of sexual assault in the early hours of Monday morning at a Melbourne hotel
Content: The coach of the Sydney Swans, Dean Cox, has spoken to the media over an alleged incident at a Melbourne hotel involving some players.Photograph: Daniel Pockett/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenThe coach of the Sydney Swans, Dean Cox, has spoken to the media over an alleged incident at a Melbourne hotel involving some players.Photograph: Daniel Pockett/Getty ImagesAFLSydney Swans coach ‘extremely disappointed’ as club faces call on standing down players linked to alleged sexual assaultPolice investigation into alleged sexual assault at hotel continuesNo arrests or charges laid; club is ‘working through everything’Jack SnapeMon 17 Aug 2026 18.56 EDTLast modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 21.31 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleVictoria police confirmed an investigation into an alleged sexual assault sparked by an incident allegedly involvingSydney Swansplayers is continuing, but no arrests or formal interviews have taken place and no charges have been laid.Swans players Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordon and Riley Bice were reportedly questioned by detectives in relation to an alleged incident at the Pullman Hotel early on Monday morning, however there is no confirmation they were directly involved.Victoria police released a new statement on Tuesday morning.Sydney Swans AFL players investigated over alleged sexual assault at Melbourne hotelRead more“Detectives from the Sexual Crimes Squad are investigating a report of a sexual assault in East Melbourne on 17 August,” it read. “The incident occurred at a hotel on Wellington Parade in the early hours of the morning.”The four players reportedly returned to the hotel in the early hours of Monday morning after drinking, following the victory over Essendon at the MCG that secured the Swans a home final.“The exact circumstances are yet to be established and the investigation into the incident remains ongoing,” the police statement read. “Police spoke to a number of people at the hotel, however no one has been arrested or formally interviewed at this time.”The statement follows comments from Swans coach Dean Cox outside the club’s training facility in Sydney.“Yeah, obviously extremely disappointed with what’s happened and understand the questions and we’ll update as we get more information,” Cox said.Asked if there would be sanctions against any players, he replied: “We’re working our way through everything with theAFLand the relevant parties, and, yeah, we’ll update where we get more information.”He did not confirm if he had spoken to any of the players about the incident, saying “we’ll speak as the day unfolds”.The matter was front page news in both Sydney and Melbourne on Tuesday, and prompted a question to Victorian premier, Ben Carroll.“It is under police investigation but every young woman, young girl, every female deserves to be treated with respect and to be given the safety that they deserve,” Carroll said. “The state government,, we have a lot of victim support services and they’ll be available for any victim.”Swans chief executive Matthew Pavlich confirmed on Monday afternoon that several players had been linked to an alleged incident, but he took no questions from media.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toFrom the Pocket: AFL WeeklyJonathan Horn brings expert analysis on the week's biggest AFL storiesEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“We’re still piecing together exactly what’s transpired here and have our own set of internal inquiries ongoing,” Pavlich said. “But safe to say that we’re extremely shocked and disappointed that this has taken place and that the players have found themselves in this situation.”The AFL has the power to stand down players if they are accused of illegal behaviour.The application of the controversial “no fault stand-down” rule is discretionary, but it was used to bar Geelong’s Tanner Bruhn from playing in 2025. Bruhn maintained his innocence and the charges against him were ultimately dropped. He has returned to play this year.In 2020, the Swans used their own powers to stand down Elijah Taylor after he was charged with assault. Taylorpleaded guiltyto unlawfully assaulting his ex-girlfriend and causing her bodily harm at a Perth hotel but was spared jail and issued a spent conviction.The Swans play North Melbourne at the MCG on Sunday. Sydney are required to name its extended squad on Thursday evening then cut that back to 23 players plus three emergencies on Friday. The Swans then have a week off during the wildcard round before a home qualifying final.Australian Associated Press contributed to this reportExplore more on these topicsAFLAustralian rules footballSydney SwansAustralia sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Arthur Fery gives Alex de Minaur stern test before bowing out in Cincinnati | Arthur Fery | The Guardian
description: Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery was beaten 7-5, 7-6 by Alex de Minaur on the day he was called up to the GB Davis Cup squad to play Ecuador next month
Author: Tumaini Carayol
Headline: Wimbledon semi-finalist Arthur Fery was beaten 7-5, 7-6 by Alex de Minaur on the day he was called up to the GB Davis Cup squad to play Ecuador next month
Content: Arthur Fery hits a forehand shot in his defeat by Alex de Minaur.Photograph: Scott Stuart/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenArthur Fery hits a forehand shot in his defeat by Alex de Minaur.Photograph: Scott Stuart/Zuma Press Wire/ShutterstockArthur FeryArthur Fery gives Alex de Minaur stern test before bowing out in CincinnatiWimbledon semi-finalist loses 7-5, 7-6 in third roundDisappointment on day of GB Davis Cup squad call-upTumaini Carayolin CincinnatiMon 17 Aug 2026 18.54 EDTLast modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 19.53 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe most pertinent question surrounding the rapidly blossoming career ofArthur Feryis exactly how far he could possibly take his game. Fery’s unexpected breakthrough run at Wimbledon last month was immense, but now he faces the intriguing challenge of seeing how he stacks up against the elite over the course of a gruelling 52 weeks on tour.Fery ended his first tournament since Wimbledon with countless reasons to be positive about his progress even as he was outperformed by Alex de Minaur in a rain-swept encounter, with Fery, the 32nd seed, making life incredibly difficult for the fifth seed for over two hours and fighting desperately until the end before falling 7-5, 7-6 (3) in the third round of the Cincinnati Open.Elena Rybakina leads call for changes to 2028 calendar after schedule chaosRead moreThis was a tight encounter even once De Minaur took control of the match. Fery began serving well, but after not facing a break point in his first five service games, one loose game on his serve allowed the Australian to break through.De Minaur, who was cheered on from his player box by his wife and Fery’s fellow British No 2 Katie Boulter, returned from the rain delay between the first and second sets on fire, his supreme defensive skills narrowing the court and exposing Fery’s relative lack of raw firepower. However, a rain delay at 5-7, 1-5 allowed Fery to regroup and he returned from the break completely relaxed and striking the ball beautifully as he dragged De Minaur into a tie-break before surrendering the match.Fery leaves Mason, Ohio, having put together another strong week filled with valuable experiences. Exactly a year ago, the 24-year-old won his first ATP Challenger title in Barranquilla, a monumental result in his career. Here, he reached the third round of a Masters 1000 with just one win, a bruising 6-4, 2-6, 7-6(4) victory over James Duckworth after receiving a first-round bye. He still earned nearly as many points – 50 to 75 – for one win in Cincinnati and his prize money of $36,110 here, his biggest paycheck outside his three grand slam main-draw appearances, is $22,000 greater than his earnings in Colombia.When players first reach the top level of the ATP or WTA tours, one significant adjustment is understanding that they will not win as many matches as they are used to, but they are still performing at a much higher level. Fery’s victory over the world No 86 Duckworth was, by ranking, the sixth-best win of his career. Competing regularly against players of De Minaur’s quality is what will allow him to continue to progress as a player.Such is the uncertainty of tennis scheduling, Fery and De Minaur already had to wait around for hours as Flavio Cobolli, the seventh seed, completed his two-hour, 29-minute comeback win against Alexander Blockx.Quick GuideFery gets first Davis Cup call-upShowArthur Fery has been named in the Great Britain Davis Cup team for the home qualifying tie against Ecuador next month.The 24-year-old, who  reached the semi-finals at Wimbledon this summer, is joined by Cameron Norrie and the doubles players Henry Patten and Lloyd Glasspool.There remains a fifth spot up for grabs, which could go to Jack Draper if the former world No 4 can get back to fitness after an injury-ravaged year.“We know Ecuador will be right up for the challenge, so to be able to call on our top two singles players and two of the world’s best doubles players – all of whom have had good results in recent weeks – gives us a great chance of securing the win,” said the GB captain Leon Smith.The tie takes place at London’s Copper Box on September 19-20, with the winners going through to the Final 8 in November.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Once they finally made it to the court, they played less than two games before rain forced them off. Fery and De Minaur returned to stiflingly humid conditions, with both players sweating profusely and trying to remain as fresh as possible in a physical match.Fery looked comfortable early on, taking care of his service games well as he constantly looked to take the ball early, dictate from the baseline and conjure opportunities to close down the net. The margins at this level, however, are so narrow. Fifty minutes into the match, with the score tied at 5-5, De Minaur took advantage of a couple of missed first serves from Fery, attacking from early in the first two points to lead 0-30.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionA loose forehand error at 30-30 and then a forehand volley error off an excellent dipping passing shot from De Minaur were the difference between them. De Minaur, who had faced three break points earlier in the set, followed up the break with a quick love hold and Fery was suddenly down a set. By the time they sat down at the changeover, the skies opened again and rain forced them off the court.There would be no positive momentum shift for Fery after the second rain delay, with De Minaur’s excellent defensive skills separating them as he eked out a series of tight games to establish a double-break lead in the set. With De Minaur leading 7-5, 5-1, they were forced off once more.This time, the momentum could not have shifted more dramatically. Fery was suddenly commanding the baseline, controlling every point and dominating against an increasingly tense De Minaur. Fery incredibly reeled off five consecutive games from the rain delay to reach 6-5, but De Minaur regrouped with a timely hold before confidently closing out the match in a tie-break.Elsewhere, Iga Swiatek continued to build her confidence and form on the court as she recovered from a set down to continue her title defence by reaching the fourth round with a 4-6, 6-1, 6-1 win over Maria Sakkari, the 29th seed. Elena Rybakina, the second seed, advanced with a 6-4, 7-6 (2) win over Magdalena Frech. Earlier on Monday, Fery was announced as part of his second Davis Cup team, with Fery and Cameron Norrie leading the Great Britain team in their tie against Ecuador in the second round of the Davis Cup qualifiers next month at the Copper Box in London.Explore more on these topicsArthur FeryTennisnewsShareReuse this content

title: Tottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario to leave for Juventus in loan deal | Tottenham Hotspur | The Guardian
description: Juventus have agreed a deal with Tottenham for Guglielmo Vicario to join on an initial loan after the Italian side decided against a move for Aston Villa’s Emiliano Martínez
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Juventus have agreed a deal with Tottenham for Guglielmo Vicario to join on an initial loan after the Italian side decided against a move for Aston Villa’s Emiliano Martínez
Content: Guglielmo Vicario spent three years at Spurs after joining from Empoli in the summer of 2023.Photograph: Adam Davy/PAView image in fullscreenGuglielmo Vicario spent three years at Spurs after joining from Empoli in the summer of 2023.Photograph: Adam Davy/PATottenham HotspurTottenham goalkeeper Guglielmo Vicario to leave for Juventus in loan dealVicario has lost No 1 slot at Spurs to Antonin KinskyCoventry and Ipswich also busy in the marketEd AaronsMon 17 Aug 2026 13.09 EDTFirst published on Mon 17 Aug 2026 07.42 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleJuventus have agreed a deal with Tottenham for Guglielmo Vicario to join on an initial loan after the Italian side decided against a move for Aston Villa’s Emiliano Martínez.Vicario is set to leave Spurs having lost his place as Roberto De Zerbi’s No 1 to Antonin Kinsky, with the agreement with Juventus containing an option to make the Italy goalkeeper’s move permanent next year for £8.6m. Martínez had been linked with the Turin club after Villa agreeda deal to sign Parma’s Zion Suzuki for around £30mbut Juventus saw a €10m offer rejected over the weekend and decided to switch their attention elsewhere. The Argentina goalkeeper is currently sidelined due to a finger injury.Vicario moved to north London in 2023 for £17.2m and has made almost 120 appearances since then. With De Zerbi having also brought in Martin Dubravka on a free transfer as cover for Kinsky, the 29-year-old will become the latest player to leave Spurs this summer after Cristian Romero, Djed Spence, Will Lankshear and Yves Bissouma. Pape Matar Sarr is also wanted by Everton and Nottingham Forest. The Senegal midfielder is valued at £30m.Spurs have already spent more than £200m on six new players in this transfer window and are keen on signing Savinho from Manchester City. The Brazil forward was not part of Enzo Maresca’s squad for the Community Shield defeat to Arsenal in Cardiff and is thought to be open to the move. Spurs have also been heavily linked with a move for Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo as De Zerbi seeks to strengthen his attack.Coventryhave signed the striker Taiwo Awoniyi from Nottingham Forest for £9m.The 29-year-old scored 23 times in 103 appearances across all competitions for Forest after joining in 2022. But the Nigeria international was limited to just three starts in the league last season and will be looking for more game time at the Coventry Building Society Arena.“I am very excited about this season, and I can’t wait to get started,” he said.“I’m really looking forward to working with my new teammates. I have seen how amazing they have been last season, coming up from the Championship. They were incredible.”Ipswichhave raided Gary O’Neil’s old club Strasbourg for Abdoul Ouattara and Julio Enciso before Saturday’s Premier League opener at home to Sunderland.Ex-Brighton attacker Enciso enjoyed a productive six-month loan at Portman Road during the club’s last season in the top flight and has signed a five-year deal with the Suffolk club. “I really enjoyed my time on loan at the club and I was so happy to see them win promotion back to the Premier League last season,” Enciso told the official club website.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I worked with the manager in France last season and the chance to play for him again at a great club like Ipswich is one I’m very excited for.”Côte d’Ivoire youngster Ouattara has also linked up with his old coach O’Neil at Ipswich and put pen to paper on a contract until 2031.Explore more on these topicsTottenham HotspurJuventusTransfer windownewsShareReuse this content

title: Hunter Bell sets sights on Hodgkinson, Werro and Broeders-Bol in 800m clash of titans | European Athletics Championships | The Guardian
description: Georgia Hunter Bell says she is ready to take on the ‘Big Three’ of Audrey Werro, Keely Hodgkinson and Femke Broeders-Bol in a race for the ages in Zurich next week
Author: Sean Ingle
Headline: Georgia Hunter Bell says she is ready to take on the ‘Big Three’ of Audrey Werro, Keely Hodgkinson and Femke Broeders-Bol in a race for the ages in Zurich next week
Content: Georgia Hunter Bell celebrates with the gold after her win in the 1500m in Birmingham.Photograph: Petr David Josek/APView image in fullscreenGeorgia Hunter Bell celebrates with the gold after her win in the 1500m in Birmingham.Photograph: Petr David Josek/APEuropean Athletics ChampionshipsHunter Bell sets sights on Hodgkinson, Werro and Broeders-Bol in 800m clash of titansBig Three and Hunter Bell to meet in Zurich next week‘I am really excited to throw my hat into the ring there’Sean IngleMon 17 Aug 2026 13.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 15.38 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleGeorgia Hunter Bell says she is ready to take on the “Big Three” of Audrey Werro, Keely Hodgkinson and Femke Broeders-Bol in a race for the ages over 800m in Zurich next week.Hunter Bell has had an extraordinary season, adding the1500m European Championship titleon Sunday to herCommonwealth 800m goldand 1500m world indoor crown. She is now ready to put herself to the test in a fast-paced 800m against the three Birmingham medallists.‘Champagne and a KFC’: how Hunt celebrated historic haul at European ChampionshipsRead more“There is still a lot left of the season,” said Hunter Bell. “I haven’t done a paced 800m yet, I have one coming up with the speedy girls. I am really excited to throw my hat into the ring there. Had a bit of fomo when I saw them on the podium. It’s such an exciting time. I am really happy.”There are some who believe that a fast-paced 800m in Zurich could get close to the world record of 1min 53.28sec, set in 1983 by the Czech Jarmila Kratochvilova, especially with the Swiss star Werro having run 1:53.80 this season – the third fastest in history.Hunter Bell could certainly be in the mix given she appears to be in the form of her life. “I haven’t run a personal best so far this year yet but weirdly you could say I’m having my best year because I keep on winning,” she said.Hunter Bell also revealed that she and the top trio had been talking to the world champion Lilian Odira about setting up a big five clash before the end of 2026.“I can’t wait for that, hopefully the big five will come together soon,” she added. “We’ve been talking after the races. ‘When are you racing? You should get into this one.’ There’s a good competitive spirit.”The most likely opportunity is the Ultimate Championships in Budapest next month, where there will be a $150,000 (£110,000) first prize on the line. “In a good way, people aren’t swerving opportunities, everyone is trying to do it together,” Hunter Bell said.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |FortnightlySign up toThe HotspotA new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisisEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHunter Bell agreed that the leading women 800m runners were like prizefighters, who believed they could beat anyone. “But there’s respect too,” she said. “Obviously you want to win. If you are in the same race, everyone runs really fast, whoever comes out on top, that’s fun. We’ll see how it goes.”Explore more on these topicsEuropean Athletics ChampionshipsAthleticsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Martin Ødegaard happy with Arsenal’s new duo and says team hungry for title defence | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: Martin Ødegaard has praised the instant impact made by new signings Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis in Arsenal’s Community Shield victory
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Martin Ødegaard has praised the instant impact made by new signings Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis in Arsenal’s Community Shield victory
Content: Martin Ødegaard was in sparkling form as Arsenal won the Community Shield in Cardiff on Sunday.Photograph: Kian Abdullah/Huw Evans/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenMartin Ødegaard was in sparkling form as Arsenal won the Community Shield in Cardiff on Sunday.Photograph: Kian Abdullah/Huw Evans/ShutterstockArsenalMartin Ødegaard happy with Arsenal’s new duo and says team hungry for title defenceCaptain’s praise for new signings Guimarães and TzolisArsenal kick off new season against Coventry on FridayEd AaronsMon 17 Aug 2026 07.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 13.56 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMartin Ødegaard has praised the instant impact made by new signings Bruno Guimarães and Christos Tzolis in Arsenal’sCommunity Shield victory over Manchester Cityon Sunday and believes the Premier League champions can compete for multiple trophies this season.Arsenal were hugely impressive as they blew away last season’s FA Cup winners in Cardiff, racing into a 3-0 lead after only 48 minutes. Tzolis – a £34m signing from Club Brugge – set up Kai Havertz for the second goal before adding another assist for Ødegaard to make it 3-0 just after half-time. Guimarães was replaced at the break by Declan Rice having put in a commanding performance on his first start sincejoining from Newcastle for £75mand Ødegaard said the Brazil midfielder has fitted in seamlessly.Arsenal’s midfield depth signals ominous warning to title rivals – and Maresca’s City | Ed AaronsRead more“Since the first day he came in, it has been such a natural thing,” said the Norwegian. “Although we had some big fights with him in the past, he has just come into the team as a real natural part of the team. And you can see his quality. He can win the ball, he’s a fighter, but he also has so much quality on the ball. He has that … he is so calm on the ball. He always takes the right amount of time and he finds the pass. It’s brilliant. Christos, as well, it is good to have new players perform like that already.”Ødegaard started 16 Premier League games last season due to a variety of injuries and scored only one goal. But after finding his form as Norwayreached the quarter-finals of the World Cupin the summer, the 27-year-old said he is determined to make more of an impact at club level. “Last season, to miss so many games because of injury was really frustrating,” Ødegaard said. “What I have just worked on is to use that as motivation for this year and to become stronger. And to use all of those experiences in a positive way. Obviously, I want to help the team score more goals, get more assists, and all that. It was a good way to start the season.”Arsenal begin their title defence against promoted Coventry on Friday night and Ødegaard expects his side to lay down a marker for the new campaign after beating City. “We wanted to show our level,” he said of the win over Enzo Maresca’s side. “Of course, last year we won the league. But this year we want more. There is a lot more to play for. We want to do it again in the league and then there are the other trophies. There is a lot to work for and still a lot of room for improvement.”Explore more on these topicsArsenalnewsShareReuse this content

title: Baller League to no longer be shown live on Sky Sports from next season | Soccer | The Guardian
description: Sky Sports is dropping its live coverage of next season’s Baller League, the celebrity six-a-side competition
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: Sky Sports is dropping its live coverage of next season’s Baller League, the celebrity six-a-side competition
Content: Baller League was launched in the UK at London’s Copper Box in 2025 after originating in Germany in 2024.Photograph: Ben Whitley/PAView image in fullscreenBaller League was launched in the UK at London’s Copper Box in 2025 after originating in Germany in 2024.Photograph: Ben Whitley/PASoccerBaller League to no longer be shown live on Sky Sports from next seasonSeason 4 of tournament will still be on YouTubeKSI’s Prime FC won Season 3 final at the O2Arena in MayExclusive byMatt HughesMon 17 Aug 2026 06.34 EDTLast modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 09.39 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSky Sports will not broadcast next season’s Baller League,the celebrity six-a-side competitionbacked by the influencer KSI, the actor Idris Elba and former players including Ian Wright and Alan Shearer.KSI’s Prime FC won last season’s Baller League final at a sold-out O2Arena in an event broadcast live on Sky. But the Guardian has learned the broadcaster has opted not to renew the contract next season. While Sky was happy with audience numbers, and particularly the level of engagement on social media, sources say the partnership had come to a natural end.Baller League was launched in Germany in 2024 with backing from the World Cup winners Mats Hummels and Lukas Podolski before expanding rapidly. A UK edition took place for the first time in 2025, with the former players Jens Lehmann and Micah Richards and the England Lioness Chloe Kelly all taking on management roles with one of the 12 teams. A US tournament was held for the first time this year.The creation of Baller League continues a trend of short-form celebrity tournaments which was started by the former Spain international Gerard Piqué, who in 2022 set up the seven-a-side Kings League, which now takes place in eight countries and has a broadcast deal with Dazn.Felix Starck, chief executive of the Baller League, told the Guardian that it had not sought an extension with Sky as it wants to make its events available free-to-air. As a result, Baller League will focus on its existing distribution with YouTube next season, although it is understood that discussions did take place with Sky’s parent company, Comcast, over a wider investment partnership that will not proceed.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSky declined to comment.Explore more on these topicsFootballnewsShareReuse this content

title: Claressa Shields has everything – except the rival who could transform her sport | Claressa Shields | The Guardian
description: The American has proved again that she’s in a class of her own. But is that a good thing for her sport?
Author: AR Shaw
Headline: The American has proved again that she’s in a class of her own. But is that a good thing for her sport?
Content: Claressa Shields celebrates victory over Kaye Scott in Atlanta.Photograph: Kevin C Cox/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenClaressa Shields celebrates victory over Kaye Scott in Atlanta.Photograph: Kevin C Cox/Getty ImagesClaressa ShieldsClaressa Shields has everything – except the rival who could transform her sportThe American has proved again that she’s in a class of her own. But is that a good thing for her sport?AR Shawat State Farm Arena in AtlantaMon 17 Aug 2026 06.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 09.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOver the weekend, more than 16,000 fans, including former and current world champions such as Floyd Mayweather, Terence Crawford and Shakur Stevenson, filled State Farm Arena in Atlanta to witnessClaressa Shields dominate Kaye Scott.Shields made quick work of Scott winning by TKO in six rounds after unleashing a flurry of punches against the Australian, whose corner threw in the towel to stop the fight before more damage could be done.​The celebrity sightings, audacious music performances and Shields’s pure class made it an entertaining night as the American took Scott’s middleweight world title. But no one will be asking for a rematch any time soon.​Boxer Chantelle Cameron: ‘If we want equal rights, equal pay, we can’t be doing two-minute rounds’Read moreShields is in a peculiar position. She lacks knockout power – only four of her 19 wins have ended in KOs – but she is unbeaten and has won world titles across five weight classes to go alongside her two Olympic golds. She’s the most renowned figure in her sport, but lacks the type of fierce rival who would help her push women’s boxing forward.Throughout the history of men’s boxing, rivalries have sparked intrigue, spurred animosity, and driven growth. Mayweather and Manny Pacquiao; Joe Louis and Max Schmeling; Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier; and Mike Tyson and Evander Holyfield were rivals who helped boxing thrive. In other sports, it becomes second nature to associate Larry Bird with Magic Johnson, Tom Brady with Peyton Manning, and Lionel Messi with Cristiano Ronaldo.Women’s boxing needs a similar culture-shifting rivalry to reach its pinnacle.After her victory over Scott – who is 42 and had just seven professional fights before Saturday – I asked Shields about whether the lack of an outstanding rival was a negative.“I feel like it’s a blessing and a curse,” Shields said. “You’re never going to see another girl get into the ring and be 50-50 with me. It’s just not going to happen … God chose me to be No 1, and I train to be No 1. I don’t need another dance partner who is easy to beat because they’re all easy to beat. Right now, I’m in my Mike Tyson era. Everyone is showing up to the arena to see whatClaressa Shieldsis going to do.”Shields’s promoter Dmitry Salita, pushed back on the notion that the 31-year-old has yet to face a worthy opponent.“When [Shields] was 9-0, she became the undisputed middleweight championby defeating Christina Hammer, who was [24-0] at the time,” Salita said. “Then she went to England and defeated [the 12-0] Savannah Marshall. Claressa has gone up and down in weight throughout her career. We line them up, and Claressa Shields knocks them down … No man or woman in this sport has the resume of Claressa Shields.”Claressa Shields eyes Britain’s Price after stopping Kaye Scott to reclaim titlesRead moreIt’s not just inside the ring where Shields dominates though. Her contemporaries have yet to equal her mastery of social media to initiate discussions that drive engagement online. When she’s not boxing, thousands are intrigued by her controversial remarks,her relationship with rapper Papooseand her elaborate style. She understands how to create and embrace a major moment that instantly becomes viral.Mikaela Mayer, who could be Shields’s next opponent, and Gabriela Fundora are accomplished fighters, but they lack visibility that extends beyond boxing. Katie Taylor is a massive star in her native Ireland and had an arch-rival in Amanda Serrano. But Taylor is 40, competed in a different weight class to Shields and will almost certainly retire after fighting in front of a huge home crowd in Dublin next month.The closest potential for a groundbreaking matchup for Shieldscame with rumors of a fightagainst Muhammad Ali’s daughter, Laila. The two have sparred verbally for the past few years without an actual fight date being set. And even though Ali owns a 24-0 record, if they did fight they would not meet on equal terms: Ali last fought in 2007 and is now 48, 17 years Shields’s senior.But even without marquee opponents, Shields has commanded attention and helped push women’s sports closer towards the recognition they deserve. And perhaps no women’s league has enjoyed more growth than the WNBA in recent years. A day after Shields’s fight at State Farm Arena, more than 17,000 fans were at the same venue to watch the Indiana Fever’s victory over the Atlanta Dream.After the game, I asked Fever star Caitlin Clark about the importance of rivalry.“These are the games you get up for,” Clark shared. “That’s what’s fun about competition. You know, you want to play the best. It makes you better and it brings out the best in you.”In recent seasons, the WNBA has benefited significantly from the intense rivalry between Clark and Angel Reese, drawing larger audiences, generating greater interest –not all of it welcome– and helping create the conditions where the league’s playerswere able to negotiate significant pay rises.If Shields had an equally compelling counterpart, women’s boxing could make a similar leap in popularity.“I think that everything is God’s timing,” Shields said after her win over Scott. “I knew that once the WNBA started making money, and I made $1m, I knew that women’s sports was changing. All of us are packing arenas. All of us have great brands. We have great fans who want to support us. And I think that women’s sports have always been very entertaining. It’s just that people try to talk down on our sports by saying the NBA is better than the WNBA, and men’s boxing is better than women’s boxing.“If you really look at it, you will look at the sport and see women’s boxing is just as entertaining. We work just as hard. We love to play, we love sports. I don’t box because I want to be like a man, I box because I strictly love fighting. When you take out the stereotypes surrounding women’s sports, we just love to play. People are allowing us to play and allowing us to fight, and it’s very entertaining.”Explore more on these topicsClaressa ShieldsBoxingUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Sainsbury’s store pauses AI scanning after false shoplifting accusation  | J Sainsbury | The Guardian
description: Supermarket chain says ‘human error’, not its Facewatch technology, to blame for ejecting a customer
Author: Helena Horton
Headline: Supermarket chain says ‘human error’, not its Facewatch technology, to blame for ejecting a customer
Content: Matt Arnold was incorrectly identified of being a shoplifter at Sainsbury’s East Dulwich superstore.Photograph: Paul MurphyView image in fullscreenMatt Arnold was incorrectly identified of being a shoplifter at Sainsbury’s East Dulwich superstore.Photograph: Paul MurphyJ SainsburySainsbury’s store pauses AI scanning after false shoplifting accusationSupermarket chain says ‘human error’, not its Facewatch technology, to blame for ejecting a customerHelena HortonMon 17 Aug 2026 09.21 EDTLast modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 18.11 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSainsbury’s has paused the use of AI face scanning in one of its stores after a customer was wrongly identified as a shoplifter and ejected from the shop.“I was embarrassed, mortified even, and felt quite humiliated and powerless,” Matt Arnold, 46, said of his ordeal.The comedy promoter was buying supplies in the store in East Dulwich, in south-eastLondon, for a standup event at Dulwich Hamlet football club when, after scanning his items and a Nectar card, he was approached by two managers who told him he could not be served owing to an earlier incident. He was then asked to leave and they tried to escort him from the store.“They simply told me they would be walking me out,” Arnold said. “At that point I did stand my ground and said I would be walking myself out. I was determined to keep some dignity. On this point, if nothing else, they did relent.”As he left, he saw an overhead CCTV monitor alert with a red circle surrounding his face. He asked the shop staff to keep his shopping in the trolley so his friend could come and pick up the supplies for the comedy night happening soon next door.“I think they were quite confused by this, understandably, but agreed and my colleague Dave went in to pay for and pick up the shop about five minutes later. There was no pause for thought from the staff, no suggestion that they understood this is not how a shoplifter would behave. Just blindly following the machine’s orders.”Sainsbury’s head office apologised to Arnold the next day and has paused use of its AI-assisted Facewatch technology in the store while an investigation takes place. But Arnold says the technology should be paused in all stores and he is worried about the extent to which AI is being used in society.“Anyone could be falsely accused and at some point that will be someone vulnerable, someone with mental health issues like anxiety. It’s inevitable,” he said. “Also, I would worry about the confidence-destroying effect of it happening to a younger person or someone less willing or able to stand up for themselves as I have done.”The supermarket chain uses facial recognition technology to identify shoplifters and other criminals, and says this is to keep staff safe from abuse. But the tech has been plagued with issues. Last September another shopper,Warren Rajah, was ordered out of a branch in Elephant and Castle, south London, after being wrongly identified by the same Facewatch software. Similar cases have occurredincluding in Home Bargainsand B&M stores.Arnold said: “Sainsbury’s, and indeed any other company using Facewatch, should disable it immediately, at least until they can guarantee the system works flawlessly. They have announced that they are suspending the surveillance in the East Dulwich store, where my incident occurred, but it’s a centralised system, so why not suspend it in every store? If there is a potential problem in East Dulwich – be it with the AI itself or the implementation of it – there are potential problems in all the stores.”‘I see the incredible promise’: on set of an AI film shoot as new studios embrace controversial techRead moreHe said he was concerned about the rise of AI in society. “I don’t like surveillance culture, but I can see how at times it is necessary. What isn’t necessary is allowing machines to make decisions and then expect humans to scuttle off and do their bidding unquestioningly.”A Sainsbury’s spokesperson said: “We have contacted Mr Arnold to apologise for his experience at our Dulwich superstore. The incident was caused by human error, not the facial recognition technology. Customers can be reassured that the Facewatch system has a 99.98% accuracy rate, and every match is reviewed by a trained manager.”A Facewatch spokesperson said their technology was not at fault in this case. “A correct alert was sent to the retailer, but was subsequently subject to human error in the way it was handled in store,” they said.The company said suspending a store was a “precautionary measure” to prevent further alerts while staff underwent additional training.Sainsbury’s said that alerts remained visible on staff devices for up to an hour and it logged all misidentifications.Explore more on these topicsJ SainsburySupermarketsRetail industryLondonSurveillanceAI (artificial intelligence)newsShareReuse this content

title: Are Microsoft’s AI plans being held back by a shortage of chips?  | Microsoft | The Guardian
description: Guardian investigation finds apparent discrepancy between what tech company has said about its AI capacity – and the number of advanced chips it has in operation
Author: Aisha Down
Headline: Guardian investigation finds apparent discrepancy between what tech company has said about its AI capacity – and the number of advanced chips it has in operation
Content: A Microsoft datacentre in the North Holland village of Middenmeer in the Netherlands. Photograph: Ramon van Flymen/EPAGuardian investigation finds apparent discrepancy between what tech company has said about its AI capacity – and the number of advanced chips it has in operationByAisha DownandEd ZitronMon 17 Aug 2026 00.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 17 Aug 2026 09.50 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe chips are quite small and some can be held in the palm of a hand. They are fundamental to the development of artificial intelligence models – and the world’s biggest technology companies need vast numbers of them to keep ahead.Microsoft is one of them. And, on paper, it seems to have a problem. A Guardian investigation has found an apparent discrepancy between what the company has said about its AI capacity – and the number of advanced AI chips it has in operation.It is not a small shortfall either. Microsoftreportedlytargeted having 1.8m AI chips installed in its datacentres around the globe by the end of 2024. Nearly two years on, in the middle of a $280bn (£208bn) expansion, the company has 2.2m AI chipsinstalled, according to internal documents seen by the Guardian. This is less than half the number some experts had imagined.Put simply, the global AI arms race requires a massive build-out of datacentres that run on extremely expensive chips. The apparentdiscrepancy over the chips suggests Microsoft’s newest datacentres may not be fully operational or, if they are, they do not have the chips they need.View image in fullscreenNvidia’s microchips are integral to the boom in datacentre development.Photograph: NurPhoto/Getty ImagesThis highlights something even more fundamental about charting the progress being made in the development of AI technologies. The chips that power AI are made by Nvidia,one of the two most valuable companies in the world. Its supply chain is one of the most tightly held secrets in the entire industry.With almost no exceptions,Nvidiadoes not report how many of these chips it sells or to whom. Its clients, the world’s biggest tech companies, in turn do not reveal how many they have. Without this information, it is very hard for anyone to know whether AI is booming or not.Microsoft: a power vacuum?In the past two years, Microsoft says it has built AI infrastructure at breakneck speed. Its chief executive, Satya Nadella, said last year it would double its global datacentre footprint by mid-2027. Since 2022 it has ploughed roughly $280bn into the land, buildings and computational infrastructure to build AI. This includesmore than $41bnin the past quarter.But it is difficult to estimate how many datacentres Microsoft has built with this money.It is possible to assess the progress that the company is making by looking at what it has announced publicly, with a particular eye on the power it needs.Datacentresneed electricity, so one way of estimating how many datacentres are operational is to add up the energy Microsoft has at its disposal – its AI capacity.Microsoft’s own claims, set out in annualreportsandquarterlyearnings, suggest it has added 5GW of datacentre capacity over the past two years as part of its AI build-out. It says it now has hundreds of datacentres on five continents.Five gigawatts is a dizzying amount of energy – it is four times the size of the largest datacentre park in Europe. But Microsoft’s total capacity should be even greater than this; it has been building AI infrastructure since 2022. How much greater is an open question.View image in fullscreenThe hardware inside a Microsoft datacentre campus.Photograph: Audrey Richardson/ReutersIn an internal presentation from 2024, Microsoftreportedlyclaimed to have 5GW of datacentre capacity already installed. That would suggest it could now have a total of 10GW of capacity. It is unclear if all of these are AI datacentres – some could be for other cloud services. But Microsoft’s own statements indicate that the overwhelming focus of its capital expenditures in recent years has been to build AI infrastructure.Ten gigawatts of AI datacentres would suggest Microsoft should have roughly 6.4m graphics processing units (GPUs). Shaolei Ren, a professor at the University of California, Riverside, said Microsoft’s sustainability reports, which contain figures for its electricity usage and are published separately from its financials, painted a different picture.He said these reports suggest Microsoft’s AI capacity in 2024 was probably closer to 1.2GW. But even this lower figure would indicate Microsoft would need roughly 4m AI chips – if it added 5GW of AI datacentres in the past two years.“According to their own metrics, Microsoft could be correct. But it isn’t clear what they mean when they say they have added datacentre capacity. They are giving insufficient context,” Ren said. “The sustainability reports are audited by a third party. They have more credibility than announcements.”An analyst who specialises in Nvidia said they thought Microsoft would have more chips,given its public statements. “They’re low to me. They’re less than I expected Microsoft would have,” they said.Microsoft insisted the Guardian’s calculations were based on incorrect information. It did not offer any insight as to which of the Guardian’s numbers were incorrect or why. What is clear is that Microsoft’s build-out of AI capacity appears to be going far more slowly than its annual reports may suggest.Ren said: “It may be plausible to secure or announce 1GW of power capacity within a single quarter on paper. But bringing that capacity online and actually using it for computing within the same quarter would be far more difficult.”Sources within Microsoft say the company’s total number of AI chips has “barely moved” over the past year.Some of the apparentdiscrepancy may be explained by Microsoft’s tie-up with OpenAI. The exact terms of their commercial partnership are not public, but this unit may account for some of Microsoft’s datacentre deployments, which would not be in the documents the Guardian has seen.View image in fullscreenA Microsoft datacentre in Middenmeer, the Netherlands.Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock‘You may have a bunch of chips … you can’t plug in’There is another factor: some of Microsoft’s big projects appear to be far from operational.Take Microsoft’s largest AI development in the US, a pair of datacentres in Wisconsin and Georgia called Fairwater. In April,Nadella, Microsoft’s chief executive,saidthe Fairwater project in Wisconsin “is going live”.Satellitefootageof the building from Epoch AI, however, appears to indicate only part of it is operational. In May,Microsoftadmittedto a Wisconsin newspaper that Fairwater was not yet online.This is very common, said Ren. Initially it was a multi-gigawatt, multibillion-dollar investment. Three years later, only 300MW has been built.View image in fullscreenSatya Nadella said last year Microsoft would double its global datacentre footprint by mid-2027.Photograph: Jeff Chiu/APThe internal document also indicates Microsoft has fewer of Nvidia’s newest model of chip, the Blackwell, than one might expect given Nvidia’s public announcements. Last March, Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, saidordersfor Blackwells from Nvidia’s top four customers – widely thought to be Amazon, Oracle, Microsoft and Google – amounted to 3.6m.There was no breakdown given for this figure, but Microsoft has historically been one of Nvidia’s largest customers. If this was still the case, that should put Microsoft’s total Blackwell holdings at somewhere close to 1m chips. In fact, it has less than half of this amount installed.Where are the chips, if not in the datacentres?Nvidia’s balance sheets appear to indicate that it has sold a great many chips; it posted a revenue of $215.9bn in February. Has Microsoft bought these but not installed them?
